meta.prompt: Rewrite Shakespeare’s “All the world’s a stage” speech (As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7) as a NEW poem in your own words: keep the seven ages of man structure and blank verse, but do not copy the original lines. Output only the poem.

text:
This earthly sphere, a vast and public stage,
Where every soul performs a destined part.
We make our entrances, then take our leave,
And each one plays through many characters.

First, helplessness, a wailing, fragile thing,
Nursed at the breast, a tender, squalling start.

Then comes the child, with satchel on his back,
A morning face, unwillingly he treads
The path to lessons, slow and full of sighs.

The lover next, with deep, despairing sighs,
Penning his verse to beauty's distant gaze,
Lost in the dream of an enchanting smile.

Then strides the warrior, quick to take offense,
His mind on glory, oaths upon his tongue,
Ready to face the cannon's roaring breath
For fleeting fame, a hero's empty praise.

The mature man then, with his sturdy frame,
A thoughtful brow, and words of reasoned weight,
Dispensing judgment, full of practiced truths,
Content within his well-earned comfort now.

The sixth act brings a figure, thin and frail,
With spectacles astride his failing nose,
His once strong voice now reedy, high, and thin,
His youthful clothes hang loosely on his frame.

The final curtain falls, a second childhood,
A deep forgetting, without sight or sound,
Without a thought, without the world's sweet taste,
Bare of all sense, dissolving into dust.
